message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds part of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control). | • Report problems in writing (email or certified mail).
• If the landlord fails to fix, you may:
 • Withhold rent (after giving notice),
 • Pay for repairs and deduct from rent,
 • File a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or local code enforcement. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease. Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are **reasonable** (no more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Keep receipts or bank records. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Month‑to‑month**: 30‑day notice to terminate.
• **Fixed‑term lease**: 30‑day notice before the lease ends.
• **Eviction**: Landlord must give a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violations). | • Provide notice in writing (email or certified mail). | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • Landlord must repair major issues (e.g., broken heating, plumbing). | • Send a written repair request; if the landlord doesn’t act, you may:
 • Pay for repairs and deduct from rent,
 • Withhold rent,
 • File a lawsuit for damages. | | **Lease Terms** | • The lease must be in writing and signed by both parties. | • Review the lease carefully before signing; ask for clarification on any ambiguous terms. | | **Eviction Process** | • Texas law requires a **notice** and a **court order** before eviction. | • If you receive an eviction notice, you have the right to contest it in court. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Small claims court (up to $20,000) for disputes over deposits, unpaid rent, or damages.
• Civil court for larger claims. | • File a claim; you may need to provide evidence (photos, receipts, correspondence). | | **Tenant’s Insurance** | • Not required by law, but highly recommended to cover personal property and liability. | • Obtain a renters’ insurance policy; keep a copy for the landlord. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Read the entire lease** – look for clauses on rent, security deposit, maintenance, entry, and termination. 2. **Ask about the security deposit** – confirm the amount and conditions for its return. 3. **Verify habitability** – check plumbing, heating, electrical, and pest control. 4. **Confirm notice periods** – ensure they match Texas law. 5. **Document the condition** – take photos or videos and keep a move‑in inspection report. 6. **Ask about repairs** – who is responsible for what, and how quickly repairs will be made. --- #### When Things Go Wrong | Issue | First Step | Next Step | |-------|------------|-----------| | Landlord refuses to return deposit | Send a written demand for the deposit | File a claim in small claims court | | Landlord fails to repair a major issue | Send a written repair request | File a complaint with TDHCA or local code enforcement | | Landlord tries to evict without proper notice | Respond to the notice in writing | File a defense in court | | Discrimination | File a complaint with TCHR or HUD | Seek legal counsel if needed | --- #### Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – [tdhca.texas.gov](https://tdhca.texas.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** – [tchr.texas.gov](https://tchr.texas.gov) - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** – [hud.gov](https://www.hud.gov) - **Texas Small Claims Court** – [txcourts.gov](https://www.txcourts.gov/small-claims/) - **Legal Aid Organizations** – e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar association referral services. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, a fair security deposit process, reasonable notice for entry, protection against discrimination, and legal recourse if your landlord violates the law. Keep records, communicate in writing, and know your options if disputes arise.
